articles.title: DJB Tender Scam Row: AAP Questions Why Raghav Chadha Was Never Questioned By Investigators
articles.description: BJP MP Raghav Chadha has denied any link to the alleged Delhi Jal Board sewage treatment plant tender scam, with his camp pointing to a key timeline. Chadha’s DJB vice-chairman tenure ended in March 2022, while the alleged irregularities reportedly took place in October 2022. The controversy has intensified after former Delhi minister Satyendar Jain’s arrest, with AAP questioning why Chadha has not been questioned. BJP leaders have accused the previous AAP government of corruption, while AAP calls the case politically motivated. The DJB tender case involves allegations of manipulation, irregularities and conspiracy.

articles.title: Karnataka: CM orders probe against ADGP M Chandrashekhar over contract allegations
articles.description: Complaints allege conflict of interest over government-linked contracts involving a company connected to the senior IPS officer’s family; CM D.K. Shivakumar has directed an inquiry and report. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has ordered an inquiry against Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) M. Chandrashekhar following allegations concerning his family members’ involvement in companies that received government-related work. The Chief Minister gave the information in a written reply in the Karnataka Legislature while responding to a question raised by JD(S) MLA Balakrishna. The issue has also added another layer to the ongoing political confrontation between the JD(S) and Chandrashekhar. At the centre of the controversy are allegations surrounding the participation of Chandrashekhar’s wife in a tender process for providing software to KEONICS, residential schools and colleges. JD(S) MLCs had earlier submitted complaints alleging that government and service rules were violated in connection with the matter. Also Read: IPS Officer M. Chandrashekhar faces fresh scrutiny over contract allocation The complaints raised questions over whether companies linked to Chandrashekhar’s family received government work through KEONICS without following the required tender procedures. Allegations have also been made regarding projects connected with minority welfare, Scheduled Caste welfare and residential schools. The matter came under further scrutiny after the allegations were raised in the Legislature. Several JD(S) MLCs, including Bhojegowda and T.A. Saravana, had submitted complaints seeking an inquiry into the alleged irregularities and possible violations of service rules. The complaints reportedly sought an investigation into the matter even where Chandrashekhar’s name was not directly mentioned. Following the complaints, the Chief Secretary had sought information and an explanation from Chandrashekhar. The senior IPS officer subsequently submitted his response to the government through letters dated June 29 and July 3, 2026. In his response, Chandrashekhar provided information about his wife, son and daughter being directors in several companies. However, allegations have continued that information about his involvement with more than 10 limited liability partnerships was not disclosed to the government. Also Read: NHAI Officer’s properties under Lokayukta scanner, ₹12.95 crore assets found The complaints have further alleged that investments were made with an intention to facilitate financial fraud. It has also been alleged that two of the 10 companies were involved in transactions worth more than ₹400 crore. Complaints have reportedly sought investigation by agencies such as the Enforcement Directorate or the Central Bureau of Investigation. Another major issue raised in the complaints is the alleged failure to disclose the business interests of Chandrashekhar’s wife, Preethi Selih Muvva. She is alleged to be a director of M/s EDVANTAGE POINT TECHNOLOGY Pvt. Ltd., a company that is alleged to have received government work through the state-owned KEONICS. The complaints have questioned whether this amounted to a possible conflict of interest and violation of service rules. They have also referred to provisions of the All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968, particularly Rules 4(2), 4(3) and 13(3), along with directions issued by the Central and Karnataka governments. Also Read: Bengaluru police nab notorious car thief linked to 61 cases According to the allegations, the company associated with Chandrashekhar’s wife received government-related projects through KEONICS, including work connected to minority welfare, Scheduled Caste welfare and residential schools. The complaints have questioned whether these works were awarded without following the normal tender process. The government has now moved to examine these allegations formally. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has directed Director General and Inspector General of Police (DG&IGP) Saleem to conduct an inquiry into the matter and submit a report to the government. The Chief Minister said in his written reply that the investigation would examine the complaints and the issues raised against the officer. Further action will depend on the findings of the inquiry and the report submitted by the investigating officer. The issue has also intensified the political exchange between the JD(S) and Chandrashekhar, with JD(S) leaders continuing to seek action over the allegations. The government’s next move is expected after the inquiry report is submitted.

articles.title: Judicial custody of five including Satyendra Jain in Delhi Jal Board tender case, next appearance on September 3
articles.description: Rouse Avenue Court has sent five accused, including former minister Satyendar Jain, to judicial custody till September 3 in the Delhi Jal Board's STP tender case worth Rs 1,946 crore. At the same time, consultant Ankit Srivastava has got two days police remand. ACB has alleged irregularities in the tender and additional loss of about Rs 123 crore.

articles.title: JKRTC Diesel Exhaust Fluid tender under scanner
articles.description: Srinagar, Aug 19: The Jammu and Kashmir Transport Department has ordered a detailed examination of the procurement process for Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF) for the Jammu and Kashmir Road Transport Corporation’s (JKRTC) BS-VI fleet. It has directed officials to produce the complete tender file and all related records before a committee in the wake of a complaint alleging irregularities in the tendering process. In a fresh communication dated August 19, Director Finance, Transport Department, Romesh Singh, JKAS, directed the Financial Advisor and Chief Accounts Officer (CAO), JKRTC, Srinagar, to appear before his office on August 20 along with all relevant records about the DEF procurement process recently concluded through the JK Tender Portal. The communication, issued with reference to JKRTC order no. 257-JKRTC of 2026 dated August 5, specifically seeks the complete tender and procurement file, including the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT), tender documents, technical and financial bids, bid evaluation and comparative statements, proceedings and minutes of the concerned committees, approvals of the competent authority, correspondence with participating bidders, and purchase or supply orders. The department has also sought the Procurement Manual, General Financial Rules (GFR), relevant government orders, circulars and instructions, besides the provisions relied upon by JKRTC for determining eligibility, evaluating bids and awarding the contract. The records, according to the order, are required to facilitate a detailed examination and ascertain whether prescribed rules, procedures and government guidelines were followed at different stages of the procurement process. The latest communication follows an earlier order issued by JKRTC on August 5, through which the corporation constituted a committee to examine the procurement process relating to the complaint received regarding supply of DEF for its BS-VI fleet. The August 5 order stated that a complaint had been received alleging irregularities in the procurement process and that the matter required comprehensive examination to ascertain whether prescribed procedures and norms had been followed. The committee comprises the Director Finance of the Transport Department, Joint Director SMG Srinagar and General Manager (Operations), JKRTC Srinagar. It was tasked with examining the complete procurement and tendering process, scrutinising relevant records, documents, approvals and proceedings, and submitting a report with specific findings and recommendations to the Managing Director JKRTC within five days. The committee was formed on the directions of the transport minister. Importantly, the order also directed that no supply order be placed with the tenderer until the matter was closed. It said any immediate requirement was to be met from the open market at ASRTU rates or the after-market rate, whichever was cheaper. The issue came to the official notice after a written complaint submitted by a Jammu based advocate Aman Thappa to the Transport Minister, alleging irregularities in JKRTC’s tender for procurement of DEF/AdBlue. The complaint alleged that Tender Reference No. 10 of 2026-27, dated May 26, 2026, had been awarded to M/s UE Autotech Pvt. Ltd at rates higher than the ASRTU-approved rates applicable during the corresponding period. Among other allegations, the complaint claimed that the tender was initially published on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) but was subsequently withdrawn and re-published on the JK Tender Portal. The complainant alleged that this resulted in the tender being taken away from the reverse-auction mechanism available on GeM. The complaint further alleged that only two bidders participated in the tender, questioned the award price against ASRTU benchmarks, and claimed that the higher rates could result in substantial additional expenditure for JKRTC, which it said consumes around 800,000 litres of DEF annually. It also raised concerns over the quality of DEF supplied by the selected firm to some other State Transport Undertakings. These claims are allegations contained in the complaint and have not been established by the authorities through the inquiry. The complainant also alleged a lack of transparency in the bid evaluation process and sought examination of the role of officials in JKRTC’s Purchase and Stores (P&S) Wing. In particular, the complaint named General Manager P&S Parvez Abdullah and Manager P&S Srinagar Siraj-u-din, alleging that they had a role in the tender-related decisions. The complainant claimed to be in possession of video and audio material which, according to the complaint, could establish the alleged role of the officials and offered to produce the material before the competent inquiry or vigilance authority. The complainant subsequently sought an independent inquiry, examination of the withdrawal of the tender from GeM, scrutiny of comparative rates and participating bidders, review of the award, quality testing of DEF supplied to JKRTC and fixation of responsibility if any procedural violations or wrongdoing were established. The letter further added that he demanded a direct independent inquiry, through the Anti-Corruption Department of Jammu & Kashmir or an officer not connected with the original tender, into the conduct of the DEF tender process and the basis on which the award to M/s UE Autotech Pvt Ltd. was approved at rates higher than the ASRTU-approved rate.
